subject: Egress IP rotation, service-account binding, and IP-caging plan for private endpoints
messages:
From: Richard Lee <richard.lee@fintrust.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: securityops@fintrust.com
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private endpoint outbound IPs and rotation schedule

Stephanie —

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. As part of our security sign-off we need the following for Redwood Private endpoints deployed in our VPC:

1) A canonical list of static IPs / IP ranges we can allow in our perimeter firewall for the control plane and for managed egress.
2) If you use a small pool of ephemeral IPs (NAT/proxy) rather than truly static addresses, we need the rotation policy and an assurance that changes will be announced X days prior.
3) A mapping of Redwood service accounts / role identities to egress IPs or to the outbound proxy identity (so our IDS can correlate flows).
4) Any TLS interception or TLS origination points (do you terminate TLS at your proxy or pass-through?).

Can you provide the above plus a short one-page justification for why the chosen approach minimizes blast radius and supports our audit requirements? We need this for our SOC workpapers.

Appreciate it — please include a contact if we need a faster sync.

-Richard
Security Architecture, FinTrust
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Richard Lee <richard.lee@fintrust.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 13:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint outbound IPs and rotation schedule

Hi Richard —

Thanks — we can absolutely provide that. High level answers up front, followed by attachments and action items:

- Canonical IPs: we operate two orthogonal egress paths for Private deployments: (A) Control plane (customer-to-redwood control channel) uses a small set of static IPs for webhook/callback traffic; (B) Model runtime outbound traffic (for telemetry, license checks, and optional model fetch) can be configured to either use static egress IPs (reserved NAT) or go through an outbound proxy managed by Redwood with ephemeral IP rotation.

- Rotation policy: when customers choose Redwood-managed proxy we rotate IPs on a rolling schedule (default 30 days) and provide a signed rotation manifest 7 days prior to change. For customers requiring stricter controls we offer pinned static egress IPs with an SLA.

- Service-account mapping: we attach a stable proxy identity and an internal service-account tag to each customer tenant; we'll provide an exported spreadsheet mapping service-account-id -> tenant-id -> outbound-proxy-id / static-ip.

- TLS behavior: by default we do TLS pass-through for customer model payloads; TLS termination only occurs at the control plane for telemetry endpoints and when customers opt into content-aware caching (opt-in feature).

Attachments included: redwood-egress-ip-list.csv (static ip ranges), egress-rotation-diagram.png (architecture and rolling-window diagram), service-account-ip-mapping.xlsx (mapping stub).

Action items:
- I will pull the full audit justification doc (one-page) and send by EOD tomorrow.
- Soojin, can you confirm the manifest format and the signed rotation policy?
- Michael, please confirm SLA/pinned-IP pricing notes for Richard.

If it helps, we can set a 30-min call tomorrow for quick Q&A.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Richard Lee <richard.lee@fintrust.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint outbound IPs and rotation schedule

Richard / Stephanie —

Quick notes on the manifest and rotation:

- Manifest format: CSV with columns [effective_from, effective_to, ip_start, ip_end, proxy_id, signed_by, signature_sha256]. We sign the manifest with our deployment key and include the signature header so you can verify authenticity.
- Change window: default 7-day notice, emergency rotations can happen with 24-hour notice if a security event is detected; those are logged and we can push to your audit stream.
- Rollout semantics: rotations are staggered by proxy_id using a 72-hour rolling window to avoid mass churn.
- Pinning: for pinned static IPs we create a dedicated NAT pool per tenant and put in the contract; time-to-allocate is ~3 business days.

Attaching a sample signed manifest in the Drive link (see related_links).

- Aditya, can you confirm the telemetry endpoints that would still reach out to our control plane static IP block?

Regards,
Soojin
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, Richard Lee <richard.lee@fintrust.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint outbound IPs and rotation schedule

Adding the telemetry/control-plane specifics:

- Control plane callbacks (webhooks for usage events, billing pings) use the static control-plane block: 52.203.120.0/27 and 18.235.64.0/28 (listed in redwood-egress-ip-list.csv).
- Optional runtime telemetry calls (model usage samples, health checks) are routed to telemetry.redwood.ai and, when the customer selects 'proxy-by-default', egress comes from proxy pool (see CSV) otherwise from the pinned NAT if requested.
- We WILL include a short mapping file of service-account -> control-plane-ip OR proxy-id so FinTrust IDS rules can map sessions to logical tenant identities. That file is the service-account-ip-mapping.xlsx attached.

Note on TLS: we never perform TLS MITM by default. Any opt-in caching requires a customer config flag and is explicitly documented and consented.

-M
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Richard Lee <richard.lee@fintrust.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint outbound IPs and rotation schedule

Richard —

Thanks for the quick review. Per your request we've attached a short justification (summary pasted below), the signed manifest sample in Drive, and the CSV of the current static and proxy pools. Next steps:

- FinTrust confirm whether you want Redwood-managed proxy (with 7-day notice rotation) or pinned dedicated NATs. If you choose pinned NATs we will draft the SLA amendment and scope a 3-day allocation window.
- If you require a longer prior-notice window for rotations we can accommodate 30 days with a commercial addendum.

Summary justification (for SOC workpapers):
- Risk containment: separating control plane static IPs from runtime egress minimizes attack surface for control signals; runtime proxy pools isolate outbound flows and are rotated to minimize stale IP exposure.
- Auditability: signed rotation manifests and per-tenant service-account mapping provide cryptographic evidence of IP ownership and change history for correlation in IDS/SIEM.
- Operability: pinned NATs are available for customers requiring stable allowlists with an SLA; managed proxy option provides lower operational overhead and reduces per-tenant cost.

Please reply with which option you prefer and any specific IDS rules you want us to include in the mapping export. Happy to join a short call if that speeds sign-off.

Best,
Stephanie
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-egress-ip-list.csv (static and proxy pools), egress-rotation-diagram.png (rolling window), service-account-ip-mapping.xlsx (mapping stub)
